Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCorp Health Systems third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCorp Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; and Alex Rivera, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: Trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, Total admissions and patient days YoY and QoQ, Operating margin guidance for the next quarter and year, Percentage of revenue from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay, Operating margin by segment, and Breakdown of revenue by service line.

These aspects highlight our disciplined approach to navigating industry dynamics while driving growth. On payer mix trends, we've managed shifts effectively despite pressures. Volumes remain strong with solid admission and patient day growth. We're guiding margins higher, payer revenue percentages are stable, segment margins are resilient, and service line diversification is accelerating.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $3.2 billion, an increase of 5.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix in key areas, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.78 billion, representing 86.9% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.05 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me dive deeper into these results, starting with trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue. Payer mix is a critical driver of our net patient service revenue, shaped by demographic changes, policy shifts, and reimbursement models. Across our 50-hospital footprint in 16 states, we've observed notable shifts that pressured our top line by about 1.5% year-over-year on an adjusted basis, though we've offset much of this through operational rigor and targeted contracting.

In Q3, our payer mix was Medicare at 46.2%, up 320 basis points from 43% last year; Medicaid at 21.5%, up 180 basis points from 19.7%; commercial managed care and indemnity at 28.4%, down 410 basis points from 32.5%; and self-pay/other at 3.9%, stable. Government payers now make up 67.7% of our mix, versus 62.7% two years ago.

The Medicare increase stems from baby boomers aging in—over 10,000 daily—and our emphasis on high-acuity lines like orthopedics, cardiology, and oncology. Medicare equivalent admissions rose 4.2% YoY, ahead of total by 150 basis points, with a case mix index of 1.82, up 2%. Yet reimbursements faced CMS FY2024 IPPS headwinds: a 2.7% bump offset by 0.5% productivity cuts and 2% sequestration. Medicare net revenue per admission was $11,450, flat QoQ but down 1.1% YoY adjusted for CMI and wage index.

Medicaid showed volume gains amid rate challenges. In our 10 Medicaid expansion states like California, New York, and Illinois—home to over 35 facilities—admissions jumped 7.8% YoY from paused redeterminations and 90 million national enrollment. This added $85 million to Q3 revenue, but at 92% of cost, with $8,720 per admission, trailing commercial by 35%. Non-expansion states like Texas and Florida, 25% of beds, grew 3.2%, aided by fee-for-service, though site-neutral policies from payers like Blue Cross Blue Shield capped outpatient pay.

Commercial, our top-margin payer, contracted with narrow networks from UnitedHealthcare, Anthem, and Cigna steering low-acuity to ASCs and urgent cares, cutting inpatient commercial admissions 5.6%. Bundled payments grew; Humana Southeast talks yielded 3.2% hikes for MS-DRGs 470-472, but commercial net per admission fell to $14,280, down 3.4% YoY. Self-pay rose slightly in rural areas from high-deductible plans, offset by No Surprises Act charity care.

Overall, this shift trimmed 150 basis points from net patient revenue growth, or $120 million same-facility. Contractual allowances hit 42.1% of gross charges from 40.8%, yielding a 2.1% drop in net revenue per adjusted admission—Medicaid at 48%, commercial 32%.

Regionally, Northeast and West Coast with 35-40% commercial held revenue per case steady, boosted by 25% Medicare ACO REACH penetration and $45 million shared savings. Southeast Medicaid-heavy at 28% lagged at 2.9% growth versus system 4.2%, hit by Florida base rates and CON limits.

We're countering with AI analytics from Change Healthcare's platform, cutting denials 18% QoQ on DRG and prior auth issues. Expanding Medicare Advantage with 15 new plans for 150,000 lives, leveraging 4.2-star ratings. Our 340B program added $210 million Q3 savings post-HRSA audits.

Ahead, Medicare stabilizes at 47-48%, Medicaid may improve 100 basis points from 5-7 million redeterminations per KFF. Commercial 2025 talks target 4-5% hikes on total cost benchmarks. Like HCA and Tenet with 300-400 bps government gains, our CMI focus, tech, and growth lines set 12.5-13% Q4 EBITDA margins, 5% revenue acceleration.

Next, total admissions and patient days YoY and QoQ. These core metrics anchor revenue visibility, showing demand, capacity use, acuity, and service mix execution.

Q3 total admissions hit 128,450, +4.2% YoY from 123,300, +2.1% QoQ from 125,800 Q2. Patient days reached 775,200, +5.8% YoY from 732,400, +3.4% QoQ from 749,500. Adjusted admissions grew 4.5% YoY including observation and outpatient.

ALOS rose to 6.03 days, +1.5% YoY from 5.94, from acuity not inefficiency. CMI up 2.1% to 1.68 on surgical/cardio shift. ADC across 50 hospitals climbed to 8,612, +5.7% YoY.

By service, surgical admissions +7.2% YoY to 42,100 via 28 da Vinci Xi systems in 22 sites—up from 19—lifting ortho/gyn double-digits. Ortho drove 15% growth, hips/knees +12% like HCA's institute. Medical +2.8% YoY, offset flu moderation by 9% sepsis/pneumonia via Epic protocols.

Observation +6.5% to 18,200 from ED overflow, Two-Midnight Rule. Adjusted days 1.12 million, +6.1% YoY.

Sunbelt (Texas, Florida, Carolinas; 62% beds) +6.8% admissions, Dallas-Fort Worth at 78% occupancy. Florida +1,200 QoQ from MA inflows. Northeast/Midwest flat to -1.2% in Pennsylvania from redeterminations, ASC competition. Mitigating with $150 million reallocations, 120 ICU to step-down.

QoQ +2.1% admissions post-Q2 winter RSV/COVID. Days +3.4% with occupancy to 76.2% via Qventus AI, cutting discharge delays 0.4 days, +8% throughput, 2,500 extra days.

Validates 'High Acuity, High Growth': Epic MyChart tele-admits +22% YoY, Viz.ai stroke +14% thrombectomies. Q2 M&A of three Tenet sites in Arizona added 1,800 annualized admissions, CMI lift. Q4 guide 3-5% YoY on electives, $400 million capex for 500 beds. Labor/RN renewals, CMS DRG risks buffered by 85% commercial mix.

Volumes track high-end 4-6% full-year.

On percentage of revenue from payers: Q3 $3.2 billion net broke as Medicare 47%, +120 bps YoY; Medicaid 18%, -50 bps YoY; commercial/managed care 28%, -30 bps; self-pay/other 7%, +60 bps from urban acuity.

Outperforms HCA/CHSS with Medicare <50%. Medicare CMI 1.85 > national 1.72 on ortho/cardio at VitaHeart-like institute. YTD +5.2% same-facility vs 3.8% top line on FY24 IPPS 5.1%, offset sequestration/Two-Midnight.

Medicaid 18% expansion-heavy Southeast/Mid-Atlantic; 2.1% days dip redeterminations, 15-20 million national losses. Texas 25% mix -1.5% rates; value-based with BCBS/Molina bundles maternity/chronic at $1,420/case +10%.

Commercial 28% highest-margin, 40-50% > Medicare; growth United/Anthem electives, but prior auth +15%, site-neutral. Northeast 35% via VitaSurg ASCs, Cigna narrow nets 105% Medicare.

Self-pay 7% rural up uninsured; bad debt 3.2% via Epic/Change AI, denials -22% QoQ. Charity $45 million YTD community benefits.

Optimizing: RCM 2.0 Cerner/Optum A/R to 42 days, +$150 million cash. ASC acquires Chicago 40%+ commercial like Tenet. 25% Medicare ACO REACH $28 million Q3 savings.

Q4 stable: Medicare 46-48%, Medicaid 17%, commercial 28%. Levers for 200 bps expansion.

Turning to breakdown of revenue by service line: Q3 $3.2 billion +4.2% YoY, 6.1% same-facility ex-divestitures/Hurricane.

Inpatient $1.44 billion, 45%; admissions 142,500 +1.8% YoY, days 512,000 +2.4%, rev/admission $16,650 +2.9% on 32% MA mix +4%. ALOS 4.7 vs 4.9 from VBP protocols. Southeast +7% surgical; Midwest flat flu. 15% DRGs bundled ACO-REACH $45 million savings.

Outpatient $960 million, 30%; +12.5% YoY 14.2% same, 2.1 million encounters +11%, $752/encounter. ASCs/HOPDs 62%; Epic telehealth +25% pre-op, no-shows <5%. $250 million FEDs/imaging 120 sites; Sunbelt +18% MRI/CT +22% Nuance AI. 45% commercial > OPPS 2.8% cut.

ED $480 million, 15%; 1.85 million visits +8.3%, $427/visit +3.1%. Trauma Level I/II 22 sites; CarePort +15% throughput, LWBS 2.1%. Northeast +5% diversion; rural +12% micro-hospitals. $100 million expansions high-ELOS.

Behavioral/other $320 million, 10%; behavioral $195 million +16%, 28,000 discharges 35 sites/units +13% days, 38% commercial. Ancillary $125 million +9% FFS cardio/oncology Olive AI.

Outpatient/behavioral 40% vs 35% YoY, CMI 1.85. EBITDA 22.4%. Medicare lag 4.5%, RN 7%; Lean productivity 85%. Q4 5-7% growth, $400 million capex ASCs/virtual, United/Anthem VBC 25%. Digital twin capacity.

Operating margin by segment: Acute hospitals 65% rev $2.08 billion, 5.2% margin +80 bps YoY from 4% adj admissions, CMI 1.68 ortho/neuro, rev/case $14,200 +3.2%, commercial 48%. Labor +6%, supplies ortho/pharma; cost/case $13,500 Vizient $45 million savings. Sunbelt 6.8% demo/35% MA vs Northeast 45%.

ASCs 28% rev $896 million? Wait, adjust to fit: actually 18% say $576 million, 24.1% +140 bps on 12% volumes joints/spines 25% ortho capture, $4,800/case +5% UHC/BC episodes. Epic ASC -18% no-shows, OR -12 min 72% util. 3 de novo Phoenix/Nashville 25% ROIC.

Behavioral 12% $384 million, 12.3% +50 bps; admissions +8% IOP/PHP 55% commercial $18,500/admission. TRM -0.8 LOS 88% occ. Southeast 14%; tele-IRT $50 million 20 states 14% target.

Physician 15% $480 million, 18.5% +110 bps; 2,200 providers 40% VBC, wRVU 4,800 +5% athenahealth 92% fill. Humana MA capitated $100 million savings hub-spoke.

Consolidated 10.8% +90 bps, EBITDA 18.2% > HCA 9.5%/Tenet 8.2%; 35% outpatient >25% avg, 15% travel nurse cut float. MSSP $120 million, $300 million M&A ASCs.

Ahead, physician fee/M A risks via standardization/contracting.

Finally, operating margin guidance: Q3 6.2% +110 bps YoY on 4.2% admissions, 1.5% commercial mix; offset RN 5.8%, GLP-1 supplies.

Q4 guide 7.0-7.5%, +80-130 bps seq; admissions 3.5-4.5% +6% surgical 150 da Vinci ALOS 4.6; outpatient 58% NPR +5% 3 ASC acquires AmSurg $45 million EBITDA. RCM AI Epic denials -15% collections 97% NPR, CMI 1.85 TAVR/onc.

Labor 52% rev +4.5% AMN float 20% fill; supplies +3% Vizient 8% discounts hips/contrast. Sunbelt 65% beds 8.2% +1.1 pts MA 42%; Northeast staffing/CON tele-ICU 85%.

FY2025 raise 7.5-8.0% +100 bps mid vs FY24; NPR $12.8 billion 5-6%, EBITDA 14.5%. MSSP 25% Medicare $120 million; UHC/Humana risk 30% rev readmits -12% Encompass. $250 million capex ambient AI 90% scribes -25% doc, bed AI 72% occ like HCA 8.6%.

CMS IPPS flat+1% 340B $180 million; commercial 140% Medicare site-neutral vigilant. Cyber $40 million post-Change; Medicaid unwind 20 bps Rust Belt. Leverage 2.8x $1.2 billion liquidity M&A $300 million Tenet SE 10% IRR.

Ahead CHSS sub-5%, track HCA double-digit EPS.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our sepsis management program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform.

Following that, Tom will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Emily. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven patient flow management and supply chain consolidation, which have resulted in significant cost savings.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI-powered predictive analytics and robotics-assisted surgery expansion, which directly address staffing shortages.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Alex. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of AI-driven patient flow management?

Tom Hargrove:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. Our AI platform from Qventus has optimized throughput by 8% system-wide, shaving 0.4 days off discharge delays and adding 2,500 patient days in Q3 alone. Combined with supply chain efforts via Vizient GPO, we've realized $45 million in savings, directly supporting our margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thanks, Maria. Telehealth via Epic MyChart has boosted tele-admit rates 22% YoY and virtual pre-op consults 25%, reducing no-shows under 5% and enhancing access in rural sites. We expect it to contribute 5% to outpatient growth in Q4, stabilizing revenue amid payer shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, David. Our $250 million FY25 capex includes ambient AI scribing for 90% encounters, cutting doc time 25%, and Viz.ai/Nuance for stroke/radiology. Partnerships like 15 new MA plans and Encompass post-acute target 30% VBC revenue, addressing staffing via predictive analytics and yielding $120 million MSSP savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel:
Given the payer mix shifts, how does your 340B optimization factor into Q4 margin guidance?

Lisa Chen:
Hi Rachel. Our 340B program, post-audits, delivered $210 million Q3 savings, bolstering government payer margins. It underpins our 7.0-7.5% Q4 guide, with further upside from AI denial reductions and ACO shared savings, offsetting potential redetermination risks.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] That concludes today's questions.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCorp Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
